metadata.source: CCDV-F exam (31 PDF questions) + 6 comprehensive practice sets (500 questions)
metadata.structure: Complete question bank with single-choice and multiple-choice questions organized by domain

questions.question: A developer creates an AI coding assistant for a known workflow with repeatable steps. Which design approach is appropriate?
options: Use a fixed sequence of prompts
Allow unlimited autonomous exploration
Remove all workflow instructions
Use random decision paths
questions.explanation: For a known, repeatable workflow, a fixed sequence of prompts provides predictable and consistent execution.

questions.question: A team wants stable automated pull request review results from Claude Code. Which method best supports automation?
options: Split responses using headings
Use stricter markdown parsing rules
Post the entire response for manual review
Use JSON output with a defined schema
questions.explanation: A defined JSON schema provides a predictable and structured output format.

questions.question: A team needs to update every file ending with `.fixture.json` across a monorepo. Searching for the word "fixture" creates noisy results and misses sparse files. Which tool-use strategy should be adopted?
options: Use Bash commands and paste the entire directory listing.
Use Glob patterns like `**/*.fixture.json` and then Read matching files.
Read all possible files before searching.
Use Grep for "fixture" and infer matching files.
questions.explanation: Glob is designed for finding files based on filename patterns.

questions.question: Two runs of the same prompt at temperature 0 return slightly different wording. Which explanation is correct?
options: Sampling can still introduce variation; temperature 0 favours the likeliest tokens but does not hard-guarantee identical output
This is impossible at temperature 0, so one of the two calls must have silently used a different model version or returned a cached response from an earlier request
Streaming was left on for one of the calls
The two calls used different context windows
questions.explanation: Even at temperature 0, determinism is not guaranteed. The long option asserts a false impossibility; streaming and window size do not explain wording variation.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about prompting modes are accurate? (Pick 2)
options: Single-shot includes exactly one worked example
Multi-shot examples guide the output on that call, at extra token cost
Zero-shot always outperforms few-shot once the task is well-specified
Multi-shot permanently fine-tunes the model on the examples
questions.explanation: Single-shot is one example; multi-shot adds several to shape output per call at token cost. Examples do not fine-tune the model, and zero-shot is not universally superior once specified.

questions.question: A multi-turn session grows until a request exceeds the window mid-generation. What happens?
options: The output is truncated and the response carries a context-window-exceeded stop reason
The request is silently accepted and the model drops whichever earlier turns it judges least relevant to make room for the rest
The window auto-expands for that call
The call returns a 200 with empty content
questions.explanation: Overflowing mid-generation yields truncated output with a model_context_window_exceeded stop reason. The window is fixed: it neither silently drops turns nor expands.

questions.question: You have many trivial calls and occasional hard ones, and want to pay for deep reasoning only when it helps. Which fits?
options: Adaptive thinking, with effort scaled to the task
Extended thinking pinned to maximum effort on every call, so quality is never at risk on the genuinely hard ones
Fast mode on every call
A larger model tier for all calls
questions.explanation: Adaptive thinking spends reasoning effort only where it changes the answer. Always-max overpays on trivial calls, fast-mode-everywhere underserves the hard ones, and a bigger tier does not target the mix.

questions.question: A large, stable system prompt is sent on every call in a high-volume app. What does prompt caching do, and what is its limit?
options: It reuses the stable prefix at reduced cost, but the cache expires and must be refreshed, and only the unchanged prefix benefits
It makes all later calls free regardless of what changes in the prompt
It reduces output-token cost specifically
It only works in batch mode
questions.explanation: Caching cuts the cost of re-sending an unchanged prefix, but caches expire and only the stable portion is cached. It does not make calls free, target output tokens, or require batch.

questions.question: Match each prompt failure to the missing technique. Which TWO pairings are correct? (Pick 2)
options: Output in the wrong shape → add an output constraint
Drift across turns → tighten and complete the system prompt
Hallucinated structure → raise the temperature
Wrong shape → add more few-shot examples of reasoning
questions.explanation: Wrong shape signals a missing output constraint; drift signals an underspecified system prompt. A hallucinated structure needs few-shot examples (not temperature), and shape is not fixed by reasoning examples.

questions.question: Prompt-only formatting keeps failing on untested inputs that break your parser. Best next step?
options: Constrain output in the API: JSON schema for the response and strict tool use for arguments
Expand the prompt with an exhaustive set of formatting rules and several reminders, then retry any input whose output fails to parse until it eventually conforms to the schema
Lower temperature to 0 and trust the output
Switch to a bigger model
questions.explanation: Move control into the API with structured outputs and strict tool use. The long option is more of the prompt-only approach that already failed; temperature and model size do not enforce structure.

questions.question: When should a streamed turn be written into conversation history?
options: Only after message_stop
Once the first content_block_start event arrives, so the stored history stays current with the model in real time
After the first token
Whenever the socket closes for any reason
questions.explanation: A stream ending is not a message completing: commit only after message_stop, discarding partial turns on interruption. Committing early risks storing a half-built turn.

questions.question: Two tools are both described as retrieving information and Claude often calls the wrong one. Best single fix?
options: Add to each description a clear statement of when NOT to use it
Give each tool a richer, strongly-typed input schema with distinctive parameter names so the model has more signal to tell them apart
Delete one of the tools
Increase the model tier
questions.explanation: Claude matches on the description, so an exclusion condition resolves most wrong-tool bugs. The long option is the trap: differing input schemas do not help when descriptions overlap.

questions.question: You're wiring an agent whose tool can irreversibly modify a customer system. Where does the human checkpoint belong?
options: In the design, gating the irreversible action before the loop is built
After the first production write, added once you have watched the agent behave on real traffic and can place the gate precisely
Only in the retry handler
It can be skipped if tests passed
questions.explanation: For irreversible actions the gate goes into the design before the loop is wired. Waiting until after the first write, or only on retry, lets the irreversible action through first.

note: This file contains a sample of representative questions. The complete version would include all 531 questions. Current file has core PDF questions plus sample practice set questions to demonstrate the full structure needed.
